verdict.reason: import-export.md (line 50-53) states the Markdown export preserves "headings, lists, links, bold/italic, code and tables." But packages/docs/src/model/types.ts defines BlockType as 'paragraph' | 'title' | 'subtitle' | 'heading' | 'list-item' | 'horizontal-rule' | 'table' | 'page-break' (line 39) with no code-block variant, and InlineStyle (lines 154-194) has fields for bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript, subscript, href, pageNumber, image, colors, fonts — but no code/monospace/inline-code field. packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts's inlineToMarkdown (lines 198-236) applies href, strikethrough, italic, bold wrapping but never emits backtick-wrapped code, and escapeMarkdownText (line 280) actually escapes literal backticks as plain text rather than using them for a code span. A grep across packages/docs/src for "code" found no inline-code/monospace concept in the model, importer, or CRDT attribute codec. This is a genuine documentation-vs-code contradiction: the prose promises a Docs feature (code formatting survives Markdown export) that the code has no way to represent in the first place, squarely within the Docs reviewer's "documentation contradicted by this PR's own code" lane.
